paper_id: Enhancing Neural Data-To-Text Generation Models with External Background Knowledge
title: Enhancing Neural Data-To-Text Generation Models with External Background Knowledge
motivation: Neural data-to-text models assume writing knowledge can be learned from training data alone, but humans consider related knowledge when writing
problem_framing: Formulate data-to-text generation as learning from parallel data-text pairs plus external knowledge via attention mechanism
key_insight: Encoding external knowledge as temporary memory and combining with context via dual-attention allows inferring facts not explicitly in data table
method_signature: KBAtt: seq2seq with dual-attention over table and knowledge base, plus copy mechanism
evaluation_criteria: BLEU-4 on 21 datasets, human fact accuracy evaluation, KBGain correlation with performance boost
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Absolute improvement is relatively small on WikiBio since 728K pairs let neural models memorize inference patterns
evidence_for_taste: the baseline model struggles to learn
no data sparsity in the original data
this inference pattern doesn't hold for this case
the improvement of our model over the baseline gradually narrows
thinking_moves: Identify that neural models fail on sparse co-occurrence pairs despite large datasets
Design KBGain metric to quantify when external knowledge is effective via correlation analysis
Perform few-shot learning analysis by splitting on co-occurrence frequency intervals
Admit baseline learns inference when parallel data is dense enough, limiting KBAtt gains
